intro: Wet rooms have become one of the most popular bathroom upgrades in Loanhead over the past few years, and it's easy to see why. Whether you're adapting a bathroom for accessibility needs, modernising a tired space, or simply wanting something that feels genuinely luxurious, a properly installed wet room transforms how a bathroom functions. Unlike a standard shower enclosure, a wet room opens up the entire floor area, creates a cleaner look, and — when done properly — lasts for decades. Loanhead homeowners are increasingly investing in this kind of premium upgrade, particularly as property values in Midlothian continue to hold strong and quality renovations make real financial sense.
localContext: Loanhead's housing stock presents a genuinely interesting mix of challenges and opportunities for wet room installation. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that make up much of the town's character tend to have solid, thick walls and original timber floor joists — both of which require careful assessment before any wet room work begins. Timber floors need thorough waterproofing and sometimes structural reinforcement to handle the weight of a tanked wet room floor, and the uneven walls typical of older stone properties can add time to the tiling and screeding stages. The modern estates on the edges of Loanhead are generally more straightforward, with concrete floors and stud walls that simplify the waterproofing process. It's also worth noting that Loanhead sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale can build up on exposed shower screens and fittings over time — one reason many wet room owners here opt for frameless or minimal fitments rather than chrome-heavy designs that show scale buildup more readily.
serviceDetail: A wet room installation in Loanhead typically follows a clear sequence of stages, and understanding what's involved helps you plan realistically. The process begins with a survey visit where a qualified installer assesses the existing bathroom, the floor construction, drainage position, and the plumbing supply routes. For older Loanhead properties, this stage occasionally uncovers surprises — older pipework, unusual joist layouts, or walls that aren't perfectly plumb — so it's worth asking installers to be thorough here rather than rushing to quote. Once the survey is complete and a design agreed, the first physical stage is strip-out: removing the existing suite, flooring, and sometimes wall tiles or plasterboard. The floor is then prepared and a new drain is positioned — usually a linear drain along one wall or a centre point drain, depending on the room layout. The floor is screeded to a gradient that directs water toward the drain, then the entire floor and lower walls are tanked using a waterproof membrane system. This tanking stage is genuinely critical; a poorly tanked wet room will fail within a few years, so it shouldn't be rushed or skimped on. Tiling follows, then wall finishing, fitting of the shower valve, screen if required, and finally the sanitaryware and accessories. From strip-out to completion, most Loanhead wet room projects take between five and ten working days depending on complexity.
pricing: In Loanhead, most wet room installations fall somewhere between £6,000 and £12,000 for a full conversion including labour, materials, and sanitaryware. The lower end of that range typically reflects a straightforward modern property with a concrete floor, a mid-range tile selection, and a simple thermostatic shower. The higher end applies to older stone-built or period properties where floor reinforcement, extensive waterproofing, or bespoke tiling is needed — and where premium fixtures are chosen. Tile choice alone can swing the budget by £1,000 or more. Underfloor heating, which works particularly well in wet rooms and helps dry the floor faster, typically adds £500 to £900 to the overall cost but is well worth considering at the point of installation rather than retrofitting later.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Loanhead and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely matters for this kind of project. Local installers will have worked in the older stone properties and period cottages that are common here, so they're less likely to be caught out by the quirks those buildings present. They'll also have established relationships with local merchants and suppliers, which can help with lead times on materials. Practically speaking, a local installer can revisit easily if any snagging is needed after completion — which is far more reassuring than working with someone travelling from a distance who's unlikely to come back quickly for a minor issue.

faqs.q: Is my older stone-built Loanhead property suitable for a wet room?
faqs.a: Most older properties in Loanhead can accommodate a wet room, but they do need more preparation. Timber joist floors require assessment and sometimes reinforcement before screeding, and the waterproofing specification needs to be robust. A good installer will survey the floor construction before quoting and factor any additional work into the price upfront rather than presenting surprises mid-project.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Loanhead?
faqs.a: For most Loanhead homes, allow between five and ten working days from strip-out to completion. Older stone-built or period properties sometimes take a day or two longer if unexpected issues arise during the floor preparation or if walls require extra work before tanking. Your installer should give you a realistic programme at the survey stage rather than an overly optimistic one.

faqs.q: Will limescale be a problem in a Loanhead wet room given the local water supply?
faqs.a: Loanhead has moderately hard water, so some limescale on shower fittings and tiles is inevitable over time. It's manageable rather than severe. Choosing fittings with easy-clean coatings, opting for minimal frameless screens instead of heavily framed enclosures, and using a squeegee after each shower all make a real difference. Some homeowners also install a small inline scale inhibitor on the shower supply.

faqs.q: Does a wet room add value to a Loanhead property?
faqs.a: A well-executed wet room generally adds appeal and value, particularly in Loanhead's mix of older character properties and modern homes. Quality matters here — a premium wet room with good tiling and fixtures is viewed positively by buyers, while a poorly installed one can raise concerns. If you're doing it primarily for resale, keep the design relatively neutral and invest in quality waterproofing and tiling.
